rca_of_user_report: Could not reproduce. Code & DOM are correct. The data-testid='download-button' IS rendered as <a href={fullBackendUrl} download={filename} target='_self'> exactly as the source defines (verified via outerHTML at runtime in real Chromium). Clicking it produces a download. Three explanations for user's failure: (1) STALE FRONTEND BUNDLE — user's browser cached the previous build that had the old <button onClick> + axios-blob approach; they need a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) or clear cache/service-worker. The user's backend log showing POST /api/export 200 but ZERO /api/download GETs strongly suggests an old bundle is still running (old code used axios.get(blob) which DID hit /api/download — so this is inconsistent with even the OLD code working, meaning the click handler is broken entirely for them). (2) BROWSER EXTENSION — ad-blocker / download-manager / privacy extension intercepting and silently dropping the <a download> click on attachment URLs. (3) Browser-level Chrome setting 'Ask where to save each file before downloading' combined with their download being blocked by Chrome's 'multiple automatic downloads' protection (Chrome blocks the SECOND auto-download from a site without prompting). The 'no download fires' part is consistent with extension or Chrome SafeBrowsing blocking the navigation entirely. Note that Playwright captures the request via page.on('request') only for top-level page loads, NOT downloads — Chromium handles downloads via a separate channel — so the backend GET WILL happen but the user's nginx/log proxy may also miss them (depending on which log layer they were inspecting).
action_items: Tell the user to HARD-REFRESH the page (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R) or clear site data for wcag-video.preview.emergentagent.com — their browser is almost certainly running a stale bundle (their network log showed ZERO /api/download GETs which means the click handler never fires at all, which contradicts both the old AND new code unless they're on a frozen/cached version).
Ask the user to test in an Incognito window with no extensions — this isolates extension interference.

Have the user open DevTools > Network and reproduce: confirm whether clicking 'Download Video' fires ANY request at all. If not, capture the actual event (right-click the anchor in DevTools > 'Inspect' and verify it shows <a href=...>). If the DOM shows <button> instead of <a>, it confirms stale bundle.
(Optional) Add a cache-bust to the index.html or set Cache-Control: no-store on the service-worker to prevent stale bundles in the preview environment.

(Optional) Move TXT/SRT/VTT download buttons to also use real <a download> elements (currently they are <button onClick={() => directDownload()}>). Today they programmatically click() inside the onClick handler which works (verified) but is less robust to extensions than a real anchor.
critical_code_review_comments: EditorPage.js line 875-886 — data-testid='download-button' is correctly a real <a href download target='_self' rel='noopener'>; no onClick. This is the most robust pattern; matches DOM at runtime.

EditorPage.js line 313 — handleExport calls downloadExportedVideo() which uses directDownload() (programmatic <a>.click). This auto-download works in Chromium because the URL is same-origin AND Content-Disposition: attachment is set. Chrome may prompt 'Allow site to download multiple files' on subsequent exports — worth informing users.

downloadCaption() still uses programmatic <a>.click inside an onClick handler (line 230-244). It works because the click is inside a user-gesture handler, but converting download-txt/srt/vtt to real <a download> elements would make them as robust as the post-export Download Video button. Low priority — they work today.
No service-worker is registered in this app (verified — no SW console messages), so stale-bundle issue would be at the CDN/browser-cache layer, not SW.
